meta.purpose: Hypothesis registry for the THIRD research campaign: non-traditional, fully-local complementary models/mechanisms that speed up or improve the harness around the configured remote endpoint (Dashscope kimi-k2.5/qwen3.7-plus/qwen3.6-plus) — targeting the pi agent's local lane and the memory system. Each hypothesis is falsifiable, has explicit metrics, thresholds, guards, and a verdict updated by this testbench (benchmarks/complementary/runner.mjs).
meta.numbering: Program-level H-sequence (collision resolved across three concurrent sessions, see 9754e02): local-llm holds H1-H11 (small-LLM lane); nonllm holds H9-H15 (campaign 1) and H23-H25 (campaign 2: ettin reranker, BM25+RRF fusion, injection-classifier shadow — renumbered from its original H16-H18 to make room for THIS bench). THIS registry holds H16-H22 (complementary mechanisms) — the allocation the nonllm session recorded. The sequence is now unambiguous; new hypotheses must start at H26 or later.
meta.method: Replay byte-faithful production prompts (imported from benchmarks/local-llm/lib/prompts.mjs, sync-commented against pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src) with fixtures captured from the live engine, against the pinned llama.cpp lane (b11718, prebuilt, CPU) and the production remote via the llm-bridge. Blind A/B judged by the remote model with position-swap consistency (reuses local-llm judge.mjs). Cross-platform validated via the C0 probe on the GitHub Actions matrix.
meta.remoteBaseline: kimi-k2.5 via llm-bridge -> Dashscope coding-intl (list $0.49/M in, $2.50/M out)
meta.localEngine: llama.cpp llama-server b11718 (MIT, official prebuilts, runtime CPU dispatch) — the SAME engine the shipped BRIDGE_LOCAL_URL lane uses, so a verified mechanism here is a `runner.mjs serve` flag away from production.
meta.scopeNote: Campaign question from the operator: experiment and decide (only if successful) about non-traditional LLM models — fully local, performance-optimized, cross-platform — that work complementary to the configured endpoint to speed up/improve harness tasks (pi and/or memory). Changes to Unown itself are gated on this registry exactly like the two prior campaigns.

hypotheses.title: N-gram speculative decoding (model-free) speeds up the local lane's JSON-heavy generation
hypotheses.statement: llama-server's n-gram speculative decoding (ngram-simple / ngram-mod — a MODEL-FREE mechanism that drafts from repeated token patterns in context, zero extra RAM, zero model files) accelerates the local lane's schema-constrained learning subtasks (note triage, failure mining) by >= 1.3x median predicted tok/s on CPU with byte-identical greedy outputs, making the async local lane cheaper in wall-clock at no resource cost on any supported platform.
hypotheses.subtask: local-lane decode speed (triage + mining replays; benefits every PI_*_MODEL_ID=local-* subtask)
guards: greedy sampling (temperature 0) for the identity guard — stochastic sampling can select different tokens under specdec (llama.cpp docs)
grammar-constrained (json_schema) arm measured separately: GBNF grammar + speculative acceptance may interact — measured, not assumed
CI cross-platform probe asserts the flags exist and the lane boots on all 3 OSes
hypotheses.precedent: llama.cpp docs/speculative.md (ngram-mod: 'iterating over text/code blocks, reasoning models that repeat thinking'; 'structured, repetitive generation - JSON, fixed templates' per community benchmarks); dev.to 2026-04 ngram experiments: big wins on repeated/templated prompts, ~0 on diverse prose; CPU-only draft-model specdec measured 2.03x on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B (inventiveHQ 2026-06)
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED 2026-10-19 on linux-x64/2vCPU/4GB (llama.cpp b11718, greedy, identity-guarded): n-gram speculation gives 0.92-1.07x median tok/s across triage(plain+grammar, n=12) and mining(grammar, n=2 real failed runs) vs the 1.3x threshold — and ngram-mod breaks greedy byte-identity on 3/12 triage outputs (9/12 identical; llama.cpp specdec is not byte-guaranteed even greedy — batched-verification float non-associativity). Novel-JSON mining output does not repeat in-context n-grams: JSON is structurally repetitive but its CONTENT is novel, so the draft acceptance is too low to pay for verification. ngram-simple kept 12/12 identity but 0.95-1.07x. Honest negative result; the lane's speed lever is model choice (see H22), not speculation. Receipts: results/c1-steps/c1-ngram.json (gitignored run dir; tables in results/REPORT.md).

hypotheses.title: Draft-model speculative decoding (Qwen2.5-0.5B drafting for Qwen3-0.6B) further speeds up the local lane
hypotheses.statement: Pairing the lane's Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M target with a Qwen2.5-0.5B draft model (same tokenizer family) reaches >= 1.5x median tok/s on the same replays, IF the tokenizer/vocab compatibility holds and the 2-vCPU draft compute does not eat the target's throughput; a failure here documents the small-box ceiling for draft-model specdec (n-gram stays the RAM-free fallback).
hypotheses.subtask: local-lane decode speed (same replays as C1)

thresholds.bootOk: tokenizer/vocab must be accepted by llama-server

guards: llama-server hard-errors on tokenizer mismatch — a boot failure refutes-by-incompatibility with the error recorded, not a silent skip
draft model RAM counted against the same 4GB co-resident budget as E9 (engine+bridge ~0.5GB must still fit)
no EAGLE-3/DFlash/MTP drafts exist for a 0.6B target (trained drafts start at Qwen3-1.7B) — documented, not measurable
hypotheses.precedent: llama.cpp specdec docs: draft/target must share tokenizer; 'target: aim for acceptance >0.6 at K=5 for net speedup'; CPU 2.03x measured on a 3B target (draft compute is cheaper relative to a slower target — a 0.6B target at ~20 tok/s is the hard case this experiment answers)
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED 2026-10-19 on linux-x64/2vCPU/4GB: Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M drafting for the Qwen3-0.6B target (tokenizer-compatible — llama-server accepts the pair, C0) reaches 1.07x mining / 0.97x triage vs the 1.5x threshold at +45MB RSS. The 0.6B target at 6-16 tok/s on 2 vCPU is already compute/memory-saturated: draft forward passes steal the same cycles the target needs, and acceptance cannot overcome it. Small-box CPU ceiling for draft-model specdec documented; the GPU-era 'aim for acceptance >0.6 at K=5' heuristic assumes the draft is ~free, which fails when draft and target are the same size class on the same cores. Identity held 14/14 (greedy). Receipts: results/c2-steps/c2-draft.json (tables in results/REPORT.md).

hypotheses.title: llama-server's prefix KV reuse cuts prefill cost on the lane's shared-system-prompt call sequences
hypotheses.statement: The local lane's calls share long stable prefixes (MINER_SYSTEM/DREAM_SYSTEM/TRIAGE_SYSTEM + memory tiers) with varying payloads; llama-server's default prompt caching (cache_prompt, same-slot prefix match) processes only the new suffix on follow-up calls, cutting prefill time >= 25% on shared-prefix sequences with identical outputs — a free production win documented for the serve defaults.
hypotheses.subtask: local-lane prefill speed (triage sequences, dream re-runs, mining batches)
metrics: prompt tokens processed on 2nd shared-prefix call (prompt_n)
guards: full-attention Qwen3-0.6B only in this experiment — hybrid/recurrent archs (Qwen3.5 DeltaNet, LFM) have partial-checkpoint limits (llama.cpp server-context.cpp SEQ_RM classes); recorded as a compatibility note for the bake-off lane
outputs must be identical (KV reuse is exact, not approximate)
hypotheses.precedent: llama.cpp slot/KV-reuse tutorial (GH discussion 13606): 2nd identical prompt processes 1 token; partial reuse on shared system prefix; hexdocs ADR-007 measured 1.23-1.31x on multi-turn Qwen3-0.6B
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-19 on linux-x64/2vCPU/4GB (llama.cpp b11718, cache_prompt default-on): on the production call shape (shared TRIAGE_SYSTEM prefix + new note payload), follow-up calls process 37% of the full prompt (median 121/301 tokens; control with broken prefix processes 95% — the mechanism is prefix-driven, not free) and prefill time drops 54.5% (1372ms -> 625ms median). Repeat-call identity identical (KV reuse is exact). Thresholds: prefillCut >= 25% PASSED at 54.5%, prompt_n engagement PASSED. Production consequence: llama-server's default already gives this to the serve lane — no flag needed; the finding is DOCUMENTATION (and a caution: hybrid-recurrent archs like qwen35 have partial-checkpoint limits, see H22). Receipts: results/c3-kvreuse/c3-kvreuse.json (tables in results/REPORT.md).

hypotheses.title: Local token-level prompt compression cuts the REMOTE lane's input cost at quality parity
hypotheses.statement: A tiny local model (Qwen3-0.6B via the lane) can select which payload chunks (transcript lines / note blocks) to keep under a budget BEFORE the expensive remote call, cutting the remote payload >= 30% on mining/dream prompts with harness-validator parity and blind-judge W+T >= L — the first mechanism that reduces what Unown pays its configured endpoint, complementary to the local lane's $0 offload.
hypotheses.subtask: remote-lane input cost (failure mining + AutoDream payloads)
guards: SYSTEM prompt + JSON schema are NEVER compressed — only the bulk payload (transcript/note content) is selectable
the compressed replay uses the SAME remote model + production prompt assembly as the baseline arm

nonllm H14 precedent respected: extractive sentence-level compression lost to the judge on technical detail — this experiment compresses LINE/CHUNK granularity with the model seeing full chunk text and a token budget, and the judge verdict is the arbiter
logprob-driven token-drop (LLMLingua-1 style) probed in C0; chunk-select is the robust fallback if prompt-logprobs are unavailable
hypotheses.precedent: LLMLingua-2 (ACL'24 Findings, arXiv 2403.12968): 2-5x compression with minimal loss, 1.6-2.9x e2e latency gain; LLMLingua-1 entropy dropping; nonllm H14 hybrid curation (19.9% cut, judge leans curated) — the remote-cost angle is unexplored
hypotheses.verdict: VERIFIED 2026-10-19 on linux-x64/2vCPU/4GB (thresholds all passed, one honest caveat): the 0.6B chunk-select compressor (json_schema grammar, HARD budget cap after the measured 35/36 over-keep) cuts the remote payload 51.3% median and the remote INPUT tokens 47.2% median (2928->2337 and 4719->2337 on the mining replays, dream 42.5%), at 100% compressor JSON validity, p50 70.8s local (async lane — mining runs after a failed run, dream is scheduled; wall-clock is not on the critical path). Harness validator: compressed arm 33% vs full arm 0% (parity+, the remote's known spec-violation behavior) — compression did not degrade spec compliance. Blind judge (position-swapped, consistency-gated): 2 ties + 1 LOSS vs 0 wins — the W+T>=L guard passes, and the loss is DIAGNOSTIC: the DREAM replay lost specific run references at 42.5% payload cut (matching nonllm H14's finding on the same seam), while both MINING replays judged tie (one judge even leaned 'compressed diagnoses the root cause MORE precisely'). Production operating point is family-specific: mining ~50% cut is a win; dream needs keep-pct >=0.7 or the H14 hybrid (activation-ranked head kept full). Local cost per mining call: ~$0.0007 of 2-vCPU time for ~$0.0014 remote savings at mining cadence — the value is the DREAM+MINING token budget under PI_MEMORY caps and offline operability, not raw dollars.

hypotheses.title: A two-tier semantic cache serves repeated learning-layer calls with zero quality loss
hypotheses.statement: The learning layer re-issues near-identical LLM calls (re-triage after note edits, dream re-runs after failed ships, retry ladders); an exact-match tier (sha256 of model+messages+params) is trivially safe, and an embedding-similarity tier (same SYSTEM prefix required + user-payload cosine >= threshold via the local nomic lane) hits on realistic replays with ZERO judge-detected quality regressions on the danger cases — hit rate and the false-hit curve are both measured, and a single loss at the production threshold refutes the near-dup tier.
metrics: near-dup hit rate at cos thresholds 0.95/0.97/0.99
judge on near-dup hits vs fresh (danger cases: edited notes, bumped memory)

thresholds.nearDupTier: 0 judge losses on danger cases at the production threshold
thresholds.reporting: hit-rate at each threshold + the false-hit curve

guards: near-dup tier only keyable within the SAME system prompt hash (cross-task contamination impossible by construction)
danger-case corpus is adversarial by design: paraphrase edits that change the ANSWER (outcome flipped) must MISS at the production threshold or the tier is refuted
GPTCache production literature warns semantic caching is 'disastrous for near-miss high-stakes queries' — this experiment measures exactly that boundary on Unown's real call shapes
hypotheses.precedent: GPTCache (zilliztech) exact + similarity tiers; truefoundry 2026-05 semantic-caching gateway analysis; the bridge already serializes remote calls (MIN_SPACING_MS) — a cache hit also skips the throttle
hypotheses.verdict: SPLIT 2026-10-19: the L1 exact tier is verified-trivially (12/12 byte-identical replays, hash-keyed); the L2 near-dup tier is REFUTED — no safe operating threshold exists on Unown's call shapes. Measured: outcome-flipped note edits (the adversarial danger corpus) embed at cos 0.952-0.974 vs their originals — i.e., they HIT L2 at 100% rate at t=0.95 and 33% at t=0.97 — while the nomic embedder's own rerun self-similarity tops out below 0.99 (nondeterministic batched inference), so the threshold that excludes the danger band (0.99) also excludes legitimate replays (0 hits). The two bands OVERLAP; this is the GPTCache 'near-miss' warning measured concretely. The judge on danger L2 hits was unanimous in its reasons ('Output A correctly reflects the EDITED outcome ... while B incorrectly...') though position-flips marked them formal ties. L2 requires a discriminator that sees the delta (e.g., a diff-hash tier for post-edit notes: same system + payload-hash-of-unchanged-lines) — a different mechanism, filed as future work, not a threshold tuning problem.

hypotheses.title: Small-model query rewriting improves memory retrieval recall (the missing retrieval layer)
hypotheses.statement: Production memory injection has NO retrieval (whole tiers, recall-qa's documented gap); with a kNN retrieval layer over session/note embeddings (nomic lane), a local 0.6B rewrite of the raw question into retrieval keyword phrases improves recall@5 by >= 5pp over raw-question embedding on the recall-qa corpus (40 questions, oracle evidence sessions) at <= 3s added p50 — the memory-side improvement candidate, integrable as an H15-style pre-processor.
guards: same embedding model + same pool for both arms (the ONLY variable is the query text)
oracle evidence = sessions containing hasAnswer turns (LongMemEval ground truth), never judge-scored
rewrite failures fall back to the raw question (graceful degradation measured, not assumed)
hypotheses.precedent: Mem0 hybrid search (semantic + BM25 + entity) beats pure-vector in production memory systems; HyDE/query-expansion literature; recall-qa README's own open item: 'no retrieval layer exists — the oracle split hands the pipeline the evidence'
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED 2026-10-19 on the recall-qa corpus (40 cases, global pool = every session in the corpus — the per-case pools measured saturated: 2-5 sessions, 100% for every arm): the 0.6B question rewrite HURTS embedding retrieval — recall@5 92.5% raw vs 87.5% rewritten (-5.0pp against the +5pp threshold; worst on single-session-user 75%->50%, where the rewrite drops distinguishing detail), at 2.3s p50 added latency and 100% JSON validity (the mechanism worked; the OUTPUT is worse). The decisive positive control in the same run: BM25(raw question) = 100.0% recall@5 on the global pool, RRF(embed-rewrite + BM25) = 100.0% — exact-token matching is the complete answer on this corpus (LongMemEval questions quote the user's own words, and the evidence sessions contain them verbatim), independently CONFIRMING nonllm campaign-2's H17 finding on a different corpus+task. Consequence for the missing retrieval layer: the candidate integrator is BM25(+RRF) — zero-model, zero-cost, 100% recall@5 — not LLM query rewriting. The rewrite idea is refuted for THIS distribution; multilingual/paraphrase-heavy corpora would need their own campaign.

hypotheses.title: Qwen3.5-0.8B (2026 tiny-SOTA, native vision) matches the incumbent 0.6B lane AND opens a local vision lane for pi
hypotheses.statement: The 2026 generation of sub-1B models (Qwen3.5-0.8B: hybrid Gated DeltaNet+attention, 262K ctx, NATIVE vision via mmproj, Apache-2.0, GGUF Q4_K_M ~0.53GB) matches the incumbent Qwen3-0.6B on the lane's triage replay (JSON validity + label agreement) within the 4GB co-resident RSS budget, and its vision projector loads in llama.cpp and answers the vlm-smoke image probe locally — upgrading the local lane's model class and adding a pi-side image capability the remote lane currently pays vision tokens for.
hypotheses.subtask: local-lane model class (triage) + pi vision capability probe
metrics: triage: JSON validity + agreement with incumbent (and vs remote when bridge up)
vision: red-circle probe answered + latency (local vs remote qwen3.7-plus)
guards: hybrid DeltaNet arch caveat: KV-prefix checkpointing is limited for recurrent layers (llama.cpp SEQ_RM classes) — H18's reuse win is NOT assumed to carry; measured as a note
262K native context is NOT the serving ctx: ctx stays at the lane's 4096 for the RSS budget
vision probe is an acceptance lane (boots + answers + latency + cost $0), not a quality verdict vs remote — a follow-up campaign needs a real screenshot corpus
hypotheses.precedent: Qwen3.5 release (Mar 2026, Artificial Analysis: 0.8B II 9 vs Qwen3-0.6B 6.5, native vision at sub-1B previously unavailable); unsloth GGUFs + mmproj; Qualcomm AI Hub runs it on-phone at 30 tok/s decode — the 'broad range of systems' requirement embodied
hypotheses.verdict: SPLIT 2026-10-19: the LOCAL VISION LANE is verified as an ACCEPTANCE lane — Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M + BF16 mmproj boots in llama.cpp b11718 (needs --jinja + chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking:false, the same H4 empty-content trap now on the vision path — 1x1 AND 100x100 red PNGs answered 'red' at 1470ms p50, $0, RSS 1176MB within the 4GB co-resident budget), opening a pi-side image capability the remote lane pays vision tokens for (remote qwen3.7-plus: 959ms, billed). The MODEL-CLASS UPGRADE is REFUTED on the lane's actual task: candidate agreement with the incumbent on the 12-note triage replay is 58% (all 5 disagreements are kind-only, benchmark->terminal; outcome 100%), agreement with remote also 58% vs the incumbent's 100%, at 15.0 tok/s vs 19.8 (slower on 2 vCPU — the hybrid DeltaNet arch does not pay off at this size on CPU) and 1.5x triage p50. The incumbent Qwen3-0.6B stays; the 0.8B's value here is its mmproj (vision), not its text lane. A real screenshot-corpus campaign is required before any production vision wiring (the H22 guard).
